source: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure

recommendations.text: Initial heart failure assessment including natriuretic peptides and ECG.

For Hf Initial Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - obtain history - physical examination - order bnp or ntprobnp (within 60 minutes) - order ecg (within 60 minutes) - order chest xray - order basic metabolic panel - order cbc - order tsh
Confirm heart failure diagnosis with echocardiography and LVEF assessment.
For Confirm Hf Diagnosis, the following actions are mandatory: - order echocardiogram (within 1440 minutes) - assess lvef - assess structural abnormalities
If BNP and NT-proBNP are low, evaluate alternative diagnoses.
For Hf Unlikely, the following actions are mandatory: - evaluate alternative diagnoses
Classify HF phenotype and document HFrEF with etiology and NYHA class.
For Hfref Classification, the following actions are mandatory: - document hfref diagnosis - assess nyha class - identify etiology
Classify HFmrEF and assess symptom burden before treatment pathway.
For Hfmref Classification, the following actions are mandatory: - document hfmref diagnosis - assess nyha class
Classify HFpEF with diastolic assessment and clinical phenotype documentation.
For Hfpef Classification, the following actions are mandatory: - document hfpef diagnosis - assess nyha class - evaluate diastolic function
Use quadruple guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF and avoid harmful agents.
For Hfref Gdmt, the following actions are mandatory: - initiate ace or arb or arni - initiate beta blocker - initiate mra - initiate sglt2i
During Hfref Gdmt, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give nsaid, give diltiazem, give verapamil, give thiazolidinedione.
RAAS inhibitors and K+ supplements in hyperkalemia cause fatal arrhythmias. [FORBIDDEN: initiate_arni, initiate_ace_or_arb_or_arni, initiate_mra, give_potassium_supplement] (Severity: CRITICAL)
NSAIDs cause sodium and fluid retention, worsening heart failure. [REQUIRED: discontinue_nsaid, give_acetaminophen_alternative] (Severity: HIGH)

CKD with borderline K+ - RAAS inhibitors worsen hyperkalemia. [FORBIDDEN: initiate_ace_with_hyperkalemia, initiate_arni_with_hyperkalemia, initiate_mra_with_hyperkalemia, give_potassium_supplement] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Specific NSAIDs forbidden in HF patients. [FORBIDDEN: continue_nsaid, give_ibuprofen, give_naproxen, give_celecoxib] (Severity: HIGH)
HFpEF patients are preload-sensitive - aggressive diuresis causes hypotension. [FORBIDDEN: give_high_dose_diuretics, increase_furosemide, add_metolazone] (Severity: HIGH)

Aggressive diuresis in HF with rising creatinine or hypotension causes cardiorenal syndrome progression and hemodynamic collapse. [FORBIDDEN: escalate_diuresis_in_cardiorenal_syndrome, give_aggressive_diuresis_in_hypotensive_hf] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA HF 2022; over-diuresis in cardiorenal syndrome worsens renal function and causes hemodynamic collapse

recommendations.text: SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended with consideration of additional HF therapies.
For Hfmref Treatment, the following actions are mandatory: - initiate sglt2i
Treat HFpEF with SGLT2 inhibitors, congestion control, and comorbidity management.
For Hfpef Treatment, the following actions are mandatory: - initiate sglt2i - manage comorbidities - manage volume status
Evaluate ICD and CRT eligibility after optimization of medical therapy.
For Device Therapy Evaluation, the following actions are mandatory: - assess icd indication - assess crt indication - check optimal gdmt duration
ICD implantation is recommended for eligible HFrEF patients after GDMT.
For Icd Implantation, the following actions are mandatory: - discuss risks benefits - obtain informed consent - implant icd
CRT is recommended for selected patients with reduced LVEF and conduction delay.
For Crt Implantation, the following actions are mandatory: - discuss risks benefits - obtain informed consent - implant crt
Acute decompensated HF management is guided by hemodynamic profile.
For Adhf Management, the following actions are mandatory: - assess hemodynamic profile - identify precipitating factors - continuous monitoring
Rate-lowering agents in bradycardia or AV block risk complete heart block. [FORBIDDEN: increase_beta_blocker, add_digoxin, add_ivabradine] (Severity: HIGH)
IV beta-blockers in acute pulmonary edema cause cardiogenic shock. [FORBIDDEN: give_high_dose_beta_blocker, give_iv_metoprolol_in_acute_failure] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Over-diuresis causes acute kidney injury and electrolyte derangements. [FORBIDDEN: give_high_dose_diuretics, increase_furosemide, add_metolazone] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AHA/ACC 2022 HF Guidelines, Section 10.2; Testani JM, JACC 2011

recommendations.text: Use IV diuretics promptly for congestion with preserved perfusion.
For Adhf Warm Wet, the following actions are mandatory: - iv diuretics (within 30 minutes) - fluid restrict - daily weights - monitor urine output - monitor electrolytes
During Adhf Warm Wet, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give iv inotropes.
Consider inotropes and close monitoring for low-perfusion congested patients.
For Adhf Cold Wet, the following actions are mandatory: - iv diuretics - consider inotropes (within 60 minutes) - consider vasodilators - hemodynamic monitoring
During Adhf Cold Wet, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give high dose beta blocker.
Use careful fluid challenge with hemodynamic reassessment in cold-dry profile.
For Adhf Cold Dry, the following actions are mandatory: - careful fluid challenge - hemodynamic monitoring
During Adhf Cold Dry, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give diuretics.
Cardiogenic shock requires ICU care, vasoactive support, and urgent escalation.

For Cardiogenic Shock Management, the following actions are mandatory: - admit to icu (within 30 minutes) - invasive hemodynamic monitoring - vasopressor support (within 30 minutes) - inotrope support - mechanical circulatory support evaluation
During Cardiogenic Shock Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give beta blocker, give high dose diuretics if hypotensive.
Select temporary or durable circulatory support with multidisciplinary input.
For Mcs Management, the following actions are mandatory: - select mcs device - multidisciplinary team evaluation
Escalate diuretic strategy and monitor kidney function in resistant congestion.
For Diuretic Resistance Management, the following actions are mandatory: - increase diuretic dose - consider combination diuretics - monitor kidney function
Assess candidacy for transplant, LVAD, or palliative pathway in advanced HF.
For Advanced Hf Evaluation, the following actions are mandatory: - confirm optimal gdmt - assess candidacy for advanced therapies - palliative care discussion
Perform comprehensive transplant evaluation and list appropriate candidates.
For Transplant Evaluation, the following actions are mandatory: - comprehensive transplant workup - psychosocial evaluation - list if appropriate
Evaluate LVAD candidacy and align therapy with patient goals of care.
For Lvad Evaluation, the following actions are mandatory: - lvad workup - discuss goals of care
Integrate symptom-focused and advance-care planning for non-candidates.
For Palliative Management, the following actions are mandatory: - symptom management - discuss advance directives - hospice referral if appropriate
Continue GDMT optimization, surveillance, and patient education longitudinally.
For Hf Chronic Management, the following actions are mandatory: - optimize gdmt titration - regular follow up - monitor for deterioration - patient education
